title: Oral etoposide · Days 1–21 once daily
purpose: This treatment aims to slow or shrink extensive small-cell lung cancer when intravenous or combination chemotherapy is unsuitable. Benefit varies; your team explains the aim for you.

agents.name: Etoposide capsules
agents.explanation: Etoposide interferes with topoisomerase II, an enzyme involved in DNA structure and repair. DNA damage can stop cancer cells dividing. Healthy blood-forming and other cells can also be affected. Absorption by mouth varies, so oral and intravenous doses are not interchangeable.
agents.watch: Call oncology immediately for fever or suddenly feeling unwell, unusual bleeding, severe tummy pain, persistent vomiting or diarrhoea, or new cough or breathlessness. Do not wait for the next cycle.
risks: Low blood counts, infection and bleeding
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea and mouth soreness

schedule_summary: Take your prescribed etoposide capsules once daily on Days 1–21. This source lists treatment on all 21 days; your team must explicitly confirm when to stop and restart. The source cycle is 21 days; continue only while helping and tolerable, after team review.
administration_text: Take etoposide capsules on an empty stomach using the exact prescribed dose and days. Do not open, chew or crush them. Capsule strengths, quantities and storage follow the supplied pharmacy label. Oral and intravenous doses are not interchangeable.
scope_note: This guide covers only Days 1–21 once daily. Do not combine it with another etoposide schedule.
treatment_scope_notice: This guide covers only Days 1–21 once daily. Do not combine it with another etoposide schedule.
phases_note: Relative educational plan; your team confirms actual appointments and changes.
timeline_note: Effects vary; no risk curve or guaranteed recovery day is shown.
safety_note: Do not use this page to calculate or change doses.
urgent_extra: Call oncology immediately for fever or suddenly feeling unwell, unusual bleeding, severe tummy pain, persistent vomiting or diarrhoea, or new cough or breathlessness. Do not wait for the next cycle.
teachback: Explain which days you take treatment, when your next blood tests are due and whom you will call tonight if unwell.
consent_support: Discuss treatment aim, alternatives including symptom-focused care, common and serious risks, fertility, possible delays or stopping, and what matters most to you.
passport_visit_note: Record the actual cycle and any omitted, delayed or changed doses with your team. A completed stamp does not authorise another dose.

support.title: Sickness and bowel symptoms
support.text: Use your prescribed prevention or rescue medicine. Report persistent vomiting, diarrhoea or inability to drink; fever with severe tummy pain needs urgent assessment.

support.title: Blood tests and review
support.text: Blood count, kidney and liver tests are checked before treatment and regularly on dates set by your team for the selected schedule.

support.title: Pregnancy, fertility and medicines
support.text: Discuss fertility and contraception before treatment. Tell the team about pregnancy, breastfeeding, all medicines, supplements and vaccines. Check before changing any medicine.

support.title: Missed or vomited capsules
support.text: Do not double a missed dose or take replacement capsules after vomiting without team advice. Record what happened, contact the oncology pharmacist/team, and follow the next scheduled dose in the agreed plan.

support.title: Safe handling
support.text: Take etoposide capsules on an empty stomach using the exact prescribed dose and days. Do not open, chew or crush them. Capsule strengths, quantities and storage follow the supplied pharmacy label. Oral and intravenous doses are not interchangeable. Keep away from children; ask the pharmacy how to return unused or damaged capsules.

questions.a: Blood results or symptoms may make a delay or dose change safer. Your team confirms when to restart.

questions.q: Are capsules gentler than an infusion?
questions.a: No. Oral chemotherapy can cause serious toxicity and needs blood tests and review. Oral and intravenous doses cannot be exchanged.
Your consultant sets the timing for your disease and treatment plan. No universal scan or tumour-marker interval is specified here.

evidence.title: Why this treatment may be offered
evidence.summary: Older studies reported tumour responses with oral etoposide. The evidence is limited, and the different oral schedules cannot be assumed to have the same benefit or risks.
evidence.intro: Older studies reported tumour responses with oral etoposide. The evidence is limited, and the different oral schedules cannot be assumed to have the same benefit or risks.
evidence.caveat: A small uncontrolled study of a 21-day oral course does not establish a survival advantage or validate all three NCCP schedules. Its participants had recurrent cancer and substantial treatment toxicity; do not transfer its response percentage to an individual.
evidence.interpretation: A small uncontrolled study of a 21-day oral course does not establish a survival advantage or validate all three NCCP schedules. Its participants had recurrent cancer and substantial treatment toxicity; do not transfer its response percentage to an individual.

chronology_notes.title: Treatment days
chronology_notes.text: Take your prescribed etoposide capsules once daily on Days 1–21. This source lists treatment on all 21 days; your team must explicitly confirm when to stop and restart. The source cycle is 21 days; continue only while helping and tolerable, after team review.

chronology_notes.title: Between cycles
chronology_notes.text: Tiredness, sickness, mouth or bowel symptoms may occur during treatment and afterwards. Timing varies. Blood counts can fall after dosing ends; fever, bleeding or feeling suddenly unwell needs an immediate call. Recovery is checked before another cycle; no calendar day guarantees that your counts or symptoms have recovered.

chronology_notes.title: Checks and next steps
chronology_notes.text: Keep planned tests and appointments. Scans and follow-up are individually arranged.

monitoring_summary: Blood count, kidney and liver tests before treatment and regularly at team-specified intervals. Scans and follow-up follow the consultant plan.
